ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the figure, the vertex is N, forming angle MNP; the left ray passes through M, and the right ray passes through P. Point Q is inside the angle, and segment NQ goes downward from N, dividing the angle into left and right two parts; the left angle is labeled (3x+5)°, and the right angle is labeled (4x−8)°. The perpendicular QM from Q to the left side NM is marked with a right angle, with length 18; the perpendicular QP from Q to the right side NP is also marked with a right angle, with length 18. Then reason: Because the perpendicular distances from point Q to the two sides NM and NP of angle MNP are equal, both 18, Q is on the angle bisector of angle MNP, therefore NQ bisects ∠MNP. Thus the two parts of the angle are equal: 3x+5 = 4x−8, solving gives x = 13. Substituting gives the left angle 3(13)+5 = 44°, and the right angle 4(13)−8 = 44°. So m∠PNM = 44° + 44° = 88°.

Since Q is equidistant from the two sides of angle MNP, Q lies on the angle bisector, so NQ bisects angle MNP. Set 3x+5 = 4x−8 to get x = 13. Then m∠PNM is the whole angle at N, so add the two equal parts: (3x+5)+(4x−8)=44+44=88.
